reason: The trigger is real and current: a $113M Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners, announced 29 Jul 2026 (Business Wire), with Cyberstarts, TCV, Conviction, FirstMark, Vintage, QuantumLight and G Squared; total funding $153M; valuation about $640M (Calcalist, reported, not company-confirmed); revenue quadrupled since the company left stealth in March 2026 with $40M ($5M seed from Cyberstarts, $35M Series A led by Conviction); HQ New York and Tel Aviv; 70+ staff across Israel, the US and Canada; Fortune 500 customers in banking, insurance, energy and technology. Honest score 64/100: timing 16, capacity 11, brand fit 12, urgency 11, ops fit 14. A company four months out of stealth, with a reported (not confirmed) valuation under $1B, ~$150M raised and a 70-person team, does not have the capacity or brand maturity for a multi-year Formula 1 partnership; the pipeline's MD threshold is 70 and the case cannot honestly reach it. The open lanes it would have fitted (cybersecurity at TGR Haas or Cadillac; no team has an AI-agent security partner) are recorded in the Zenity case (N° 155), a direct rival with Gartner's 'company to beat' verdict, 230 staff and ~$185M raised, which was built instead. Re-run if Onyx confirms a $1B+ round or names a CMO.
